__inputs.name: DS_PROMETHEUS
__inputs.label: Prometheus
__inputs.description: Prometheus data source scraping the orleans.lattice (and optionally orleans.lattice.replication) meter.

panels.title: Commit-step latency p95 (ms) - wal / apply / observer / digest
Activation replay duration p95 by outcome (ms)

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, outcome) (rate(orleans_lattice_leaf_replay_duration_milliseconds_bucket{tree=~"$tree",cluster=~"$cluster",instance=~"$silo"}[10m]))) or vector(0)

panels.title: SetAsync / SetManyAsync envelope p50 (ms)
panels.description: Top-of-stack public-API call duration: set.duration is single-key SetAsync, set_many.duration is bulk SetManyAsync. Pairs with the stage-breakdown panels below to attribute envelope cost to gate / route / bucket / shard / publish.

panels.title: SetAsync / SetManyAsync envelope p95 (ms)
panels.description: p95 of the public-API call envelopes. The gap between p50 and p95 here is the tail introduced by stale-routing retries, registry probes, or contended placement-directory lookups.

panels.title: SetAsync stage breakdown p95 (ms)
panels.description: Per-stage sub-attribution inside LatticeGrain.SetAsync. set.stage.duration is tagged stage = shard (inner shard.SetAsync RPC including stale-routing retries) and stage = publish (trailing PublishEventAsync hop).

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, stage) (rate(orleans_lattice_set_stage_duration_milliseconds_bucket{tree=~"$tree",cluster=~"$cluster",instance=~"$silo"}[5m]))) or vector(0)

panels.title: SetManyAsync stage breakdown p95 (ms)
panels.description: Per-stage sub-attribution inside LatticeGrain.SetManyAsync. set_many.stage.duration is tagged stage in {gate, route, bucket, fanout, events}, isolating pre-flight gating, routing fetch, per-key bucketing, per-shard fan-out, and trailing event publication.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, stage) (rate(orleans_lattice_set_many_stage_duration_milliseconds_bucket{tree=~"$tree",cluster=~"$cluster",instance=~"$silo"}[5m]))) or vector(0)

panels.title: ShardRoot.SetMany sub-attribution p95 (ms)
panels.description: Per-step latency inside ShardRootGrain.SetManyLocalOnlyAsync: local_apply (per-leaf parallel dispatch), shadow_forward (mid-split forward to destination shard), and leaf_rpc (the actual per-leaf SetManyAsync RPC envelope).

panels.title: WAL append latency p95 (ms) - turn-wait / provider / dispatch
panels.description: Decomposed WAL-append cost: turn_wait (time spent in the WalShardGrain turn queue before the append runs), provider.duration (storage-provider append latency), dispatch.duration (caller-side cross-grain RPC envelope - turn_wait + provider + Orleans transport). dispatch - (turn_wait + provider) approximates Orleans transport overhead per partition.

panels.title: WAL batch shape p95 - entries / bytes / dispatch-entries
panels.description: Per-flush batch shape. wal.append.batch_entries / batch_bytes are the per-flush sizes at the WalShardGrain (sized to WalMaxBatchEntries / WalMaxBatchBytes). wal.shard.dispatch.entries is the caller-side per-RPC batch size (=1 for single AppendAsync, N for AppendManyAsync). A persistent batch_entries p95 = 1 indicates the producer is not actually saturating the WAL flush envelope and coalescing is wasted.

panels.title: WAL pipeline depth p95 - in-flight flushes / queue depth
panels.description: Back-pressure indicators on WalShardGrain. wal.append.in_flight is the number of concurrent provider flushes (capped at WalMaxPendingBatches). wal.append.queue_depth is the in-grain pending-entry depth before flush. Pinned in-flight at the cap with growing queue_depth indicates the cap is saturated and a higher WalMaxPendingBatches could lift throughput; queue_depth = 0 with in-flight < cap indicates the producer side is the binding constraint.

panels.title: Storage-provider phase-2 commit p95 (ms) + batch size
panels.description: provider.commit.duration is the storage-provider's phase-2 commit latency. provider.phase2.batch_size is the per-commit entry count (= 1 on every commit means the provider's coalescing window never traps a second arrival; raise the coalescing window if throughput is bound).

panels.title: Storage-provider retries (ops/s) - attempts vs exhausted vs idempotent-replays vs phase1-transient
panels.description: provider.retry.attempts tracks every retry the storage adapter issues against a transient failure (healthy resilience under transient-fault load). provider.retry.exhausted increments when the bounded-retry budget is exhausted and the caller-visible exception propagates - any non-zero rate is alert-worthy because it means a foreground commit failed. provider.idempotent_replays increments when a phase-one batch hits a 409 EntityAlreadyExists whose resident rows are proven byte-identical to the batch (a lost-response SDK retry of an already-durable write) and is resolved as a success - a non-zero rate is benign but signals the cluster is losing phase-one responses under load (CPU / network pressure), so it should track alongside, not instead of, exhausted. provider.phase1.transient_retries counts phase-1 commit attempts the provider re-issued in place after a transient fault, resubmitting the byte-identical batch at the same offsets rather than faulting the calling WAL shard - a non-zero rate means the provider absorbed phase-1 turbulence without escalating it to the shard.

panels.title: Leaf commit concurrency (in-flight) p95
panels.description: Snapshot of in-flight foreground commits on a single BPlusLeafGrain at the moment a new commit enters the commit path. Pins at 0 under the default non-reentrant grain shape; a sustained non-zero tail tracks contention from saga-prepare arrivals or producer-side fan-in.

panels.title: WarmUpAsync - invocations and duration
panels.description: ILattice.WarmUpAsync per-call cost and rate. A non-zero invocation rate after the cluster has warmed up indicates the host is re-warming on every request (a configuration bug); duration is the wall-clock cost of routing resolution plus the bounded-concurrency per-shard probe round-trip.

panels.title: Digest publish path attribution (ops/s) - coalescing efficacy
panels.description: leaf.digest.publishes tagged path = {coalesced_scheduled, coalesced_skipped, coalesced_fired, inline, deactivation_flush}. Headline coalescing invariant: coalesced_skipped/(scheduled+skipped) is the ratio of writes that avoided a parent RPC; coalesced_fired is the actual per-window cross-grain hop. A regression to the c2-xxix shape (resolver dropping DigestCoalescingWindowMs) shows up as zero coalesced_* rates and inline rising in lockstep with writes.

panels.title: Shard-forward timeouts (ops/s) - reshard swap-phase wedge guard
panels.description: shard_root.forward.timeouts is the rate of outbound shard-to-shard write forwards abandoned after exceeding ShardForwardTimeout. Zero in steady state. A sustained non-zero rate during a resize means a forward parked against a sibling shard whose ownership was changing during the reshard swap; the forward was faulted as a TimeoutException so the foreground write pipeline could make progress and the write retried against refreshed routing. A persistent non-zero rate outside a resize window indicates the swap phase is outlasting the configured forward deadline.

panels.title: Leaf-cache pre-warm (opt-in) - leaves primed, fan-out cost, model size
panels.description: Post-restart LeafCacheGrain pre-warm, driven by each shard root's persisted leaf-access frequency histogram (LatticeOptions.LeafCachePreWarmCount, default 0 = disabled). warmup.leaf_cache.prewarmed is leaves successfully primed; a rate materially below shards x LeafCachePreWarmCount per warm-up means individual priming calls are failing (they are swallowed by design, so this counter is the only signal). warmup.leaf_cache.duration is the per-shard fan-out cost, read against warmup.duration to attribute how much of warm-up is leaf priming. leaf_access.model.leaves is the resident model size at persist time; a distribution pinned at the model's tracked-leaf cap means the shard's read set is wider than the model represents and the ranking is drawn from a pruned view. All three stay flat at zero while the feature is disabled.

panels.title: WAL writer admission & dispatch (rate)
panels.description: Outbound WAL writer admission outcomes and dispatch rate: admission_saturation_refusals (writer refused an append because the per-partition admission cap was saturated), admission_timeouts (waiter timed out before admission), dispatched (appends handed to the provider) and drain.releases (admission slots released on drain). A rising refusal/timeout rate is the writer-tier view of WAL back-pressure.

panels.title: WAL writer admission wait p50/p95/p99 (ms)
panels.description: Time an append waits for an admission slot before being dispatched (orleans.lattice.wal.writer.append.admission_wait). The latency twin of the admission counters: a climbing p95 is the early warning that the writer is becoming the commit-path bottleneck.

panels.title: WAL writer partition pending appends (p50/p95/max)
panels.description: Distribution of queued appends per WAL writer partition (orleans.lattice.wal.writer.partition.pending_appends). A persistently high max with a low p50 indicates a single hot partition; a uniformly high distribution indicates a cluster-wide write cap.

panels.title: WAL shard backlog (p95)
panels.description: Per-shard WAL backlog gauges at p95: pending_segments (unflushed segments), deactivate.in_flight (slots awaiting deactivation), drain.budget.force_faulted_slots (slots force-faulted when the drain budget expired). Sustained growth precedes a saturation regime.

panels.title: WAL shard drain budget & flush calls (rate)
panels.description: Rate of WAL shard drain-budget expirations (orleans.lattice.wal.shard.drain.budget.expirations) and start-flush calls (orleans.lattice.wal.shard.start_flush.calls). Budget expirations are the trigger for the force-faulted-slots backlog above; a non-zero rate means drains are not completing within WalDrainBudget.

panels.title: WAL flush / dispatch timeouts (rate)
panels.description: Rate of WAL timeout trips: append_dispatch.timeouts (an append-dispatch turn exceeded WalAppendDispatchTimeout) and flush.preflight.timeouts (a flush preflight exceeded WalFlushPreflightTimeout). Each non-zero series is a deadline guard firing and should be rare in a healthy silo.

panels.title: Provider commit timeouts & retry short-circuits (rate)
panels.description: Rate of storage-provider commit timeouts (orleans.lattice.provider.phase2.commit.timeouts) and retry short-circuits (orleans.lattice.provider.retry.short_circuited, a retry abandoned early because the circuit was open). Both are provider-health signals on the commit path.

panels.title: Digest reads & publish timeouts (rate)
panels.description: Rate of leaf-digest reads (orleans.lattice.shard.digest_reads) and internal digest-publish timeouts (orleans.lattice.internal.digest_publish.timeouts, a digest publish that exceeded DigestPublishTimeout). The timeout series should stay flat-zero in a healthy cluster.

panels.title: Reshard activity (rate)
panels.description: Rate of online-reshard lifecycle events: initiated, completed, rejected (orleans.lattice.shard_root.reshard.*) and activation_ready.timeouts (orleans.lattice.shard_root.activation_ready.timeouts, a shard activation that did not become ready within ActivationReadyTimeout). Rejections and activation-ready timeouts should be rare.

panels.title: Reshard runs in flight (p50/p95/max)
panels.description: Distribution of concurrent in-flight reshard runs (orleans.lattice.shard_root.reshard.in_flight). The companion gauge to the reshard activity counters; a non-zero max means a resize is actively migrating slots.

panels.title: Leaf-materialiser durable pin path (rate) - issue #1030
panels.description: Health of the durable leaf-materialiser pin store (issue #1030 fan-in hotspot fix). durable_writes by outcome (birth = synchronous through-write at leaf birth; coalesced = debounced flush draining advancing reports) - a coalesced rate far below the activation_replays rate confirms write coalescing is collapsing the report burst. activation_replays is the per-silo leaf reactivation rate; cursor_publish_failures should stay flat-zero (a non-zero rate signals reactivation-storm pressure). activation_replays_over_budget counts cold replays that exceeded MaxLeafReplayEntries with an intact WAL (issue #1738) - these converge normally, so a sustained rate is a capacity signal that the materialiser is checkpointing too slowly for the write rate, not a fault.

panels.title: Leaf-materialiser drain lag p50/p95 (ms) - issue #1030 back-pressure
panels.description: Distribution of leaf-materialiser drain lag (orleans.lattice.materialiser.drain_lag), sampled by each per-tree WAL GC pass as now minus the slowest durable materialiser checkpoint. This is the drain-lag back-pressure signal: when it exceeds WalSaturationMaterialiserLagThreshold for WalSaturationMaterialiserLagSampleWindows consecutive passes the tree escalates to Saturated and the writer admission gate plus replication flow control throttle. A sustained climb here is the early warning the wedge is forming.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (le, tree) (rate(orleans_lattice_materialiser_drain_lag_bucket{tree=~"$tree",cluster=~"$cluster",instance=~"$silo"}[5m]))) or vector(0)
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, tree) (rate(orleans_lattice_materialiser_drain_lag_bucket{tree=~"$tree",cluster=~"$cluster",instance=~"$silo"}[5m]))) or vector(0)

panels.title: Mutation-observer inline latency p95 (ms) by observer
panels.description: Per-observer breakdown of the inline IMutationObserver callback cost (orleans.lattice.observer.duration), split by the observer CLR type. Observers run inline on the write path, so this is latency the caller pays: it is the by-observer decomposition of the aggregate observer step on the Commit-step latency panel above. A single series climbing away from its peers names the misbehaving observer (synchronous I/O, a blocking call, a chatty downstream). The measurement is taken on the faulting path too, so an observer that throws slowly still shows up here.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, observer) (rate(orleans_lattice_observer_duration_milliseconds_bucket{tree=~"$tree",cluster=~"$cluster",instance=~"$silo"}[5m]))) or vector(0)
histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (le, observer) (rate(orleans_lattice_observer_duration_milliseconds_bucket{tree=~"$tree",cluster=~"$cluster",instance=~"$silo"}[5m]))) or vector(0)
